I'll help you understand and fix the import error in your Setzer application. Let's analyze the issue.Based on the error message and my analysis of the code, I can identify the issue and provide a solution.
## Analysis of the Problem
Looking at the error message: ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/Setzer2/main.py", line 24, in <module> from workspace.workspace import Workspace File "/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/Setzer2/workspace/workspace.py", line 23, in <module> from setzer.document.document import Document ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setzer' ```
The issue is in the import statement in the workspace.py file. The code is trying to import the Document class from `setzer.document.document`, but there is no module named 'setzer' in the project structure. Instead, the Document class should be imported directly from the document module that exists in the project.
## Solution
The fix is to correct the import statement in workspace.py to use the correct path to the Document class based on the actual project structure. Instead of importing from `setzer.document.document`, it should import from `document.document`.
```python # Fix for workspace.py from document.document import Document ```
Here's the complete solution:
```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # coding: utf-8
# Copyright (C) 2017-present Robert Griesel # This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify # it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by # the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or # (at your option) any later version. # # This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, # but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of # MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the # GNU General Public License for more details. # # You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License # along with this program. If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>
import sys import gi gi.require_version('Gtk', '4.0') from gi.repository import Gtk, GLib, Gio
from app.service_locator import ServiceLocator from workspace.workspace import Workspace
import time
class WorkspaceController(object): ''' Mediator between workspace and view. '''
def __init__(self, workspace):
self.workspace = workspace self.main_window = ServiceLocator.get_main_window()
self.main_window.headerbar.preview_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_preview_toggle_toggled) self.main_window.headerbar.help_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_help_toggle_toggled)
self.main_window.headerbar.document_structure_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_document_structure_toggle_toggled) self.main_window.headerbar.symbols_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_symbols_toggle_toggled)
# populate workspace self.workspace.populate_from_disk() open_documents = self.workspace.open_documents if len(open_documents) > 0: self.workspace.set_active_document(open_documents[-1])
def on_preview_toggle_toggled(self, toggle_button, parameter=None): show_preview = toggle_button.get_active() if show_preview: show_help = False else: show_help = self.workspace.show_help self.workspace.set_show_preview_or_help(show_preview, show_help)
if show_preview: self.main_window.headerbar.help_toggle.set_active(False)
def on_help_toggle_toggled(self, toggle_button, parameter=None): show_help = toggle_button.get_active() if show_help: show_preview = False else: show_preview = self.workspace.show_preview self.workspace.set_show_preview_or_help(show_preview, show_help)
if show_help: self.main_window.headerbar.preview_toggle.set_active(False)
def on_document_structure_toggle_toggled(self, toggle_button, parameter=None): show_document_structure = toggle_button.get_active() if show_document_structure: show_symbols = False else: show_symbols = self.workspace.show_symbols self.workspace.set_show_symbols_or_document_structure(show_symbols, show_document_structure)
if show_document_structure: self.main_window.headerbar.symbols_toggle.set_active(False)
def on_symbols_toggle_toggled(self, toggle_button, parameter=None): show_symbols = toggle_button.get_active() if show_symbols: show_document_structure = False else: show_document_structure = self.workspace.show_document_structure self.workspace.set_show_symbols_or_document_structure(show_symbols, show_document_structure)
if show_symbols: self.main_window.headerbar.document_structure_toggle.set_active(False)
class SetzerApplication(Gtk.Application): """Main application class for Setzer"""
def __init__(self): super().__init__(application_id="org.setzer.app", flags=Gio.ApplicationFlags.FLAGS_NONE)
def do_activate(self): # Initialize application services ServiceLocator.init_services()
# Create the main window main_window = ServiceLocator.get_main_window() self.add_window(main_window) main_window.present()
# Initialize workspace workspace = Workspace() self.controller = WorkspaceController(workspace)
if __name__ == "__main__": app = SetzerApplication() exit_status = app.run(sys.argv) sys.exit(exit_status) ```
The fix for the workspace.py file would be:
```python # In workspace.py, line 23 # Change from: from setzer.document.document import Document # To: from document.document import Document ```
This change ensures that the Document class is imported from the correct location according to the project structure, resolving the ModuleNotFoundError.

* **Optimize imports on the fly**: IntelliJ IDEA will optimize imports as you work. [[1]](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/2025.1/creating-and-optimizing-imports.html#pzprsy_151) - Press `Ctrl` + `Alt` + `S` to open settings. <ActionButton id="ShowSettings"/> - Go to **Editor | General | Auto Import**. <ActionButton id="ShowSettings" value="Editor | General | Auto Import"/> - Enable the **Optimize imports on the fly** option. - Apply the changes.
* **Optimize imports on save**: IntelliJ IDEA will optimize imports when you save the file. This should help you keep your Python imports clean and organized in `document.py`.

option.value:
I'll help you identify and fix the problem in your code.
## Analysis:
Looking at the error message, the issue is a circular import problem. The error states that `document` is not a package, but the import statement is trying to use it as one with `import document.document_controller as document_controller`.
## Steps:
1. Check if the import is trying to import from itself, causing a circular import 2. Determine if the module structure is properly set up as a package 3. Fix the import statement to correctly reference the document_controller module
## Patches:
<llm-patch path="/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/Setzer2/document/document.py" matcher="BeforeAfter"> Fix circular import by changing relative import <!--Separator--> Before: ```python import os.path, time
import document.document_controller as document_controller import document.document_presenter as document_presenter import document.document_viewgtk as document_view import document.search.search as search import document.gutter.gutter as gutter import document.parser.parser_latex as parser_latex import document.parser.parser_bibtex as parser_bibtex import document.parser.parser_dummy as parser_dummy import document.code_folding.code_folding as code_folding import document.bracket_completion.bracket_completion as bracket_completion ```
After: ```python import os.path, time
# Use relative imports since we're in the document module already from . import document_controller from . import document_presenter from . import document_viewgtk as document_view from .search import search from .gutter import gutter from .parser import parser_latex, parser_bibtex, parser_dummy from .code_folding import code_folding from .bracket_completion import bracket_completion ``` </llm-patch>
<llm-patch path="/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/Setzer2/document/document.py" matcher="BeforeAfter"> Fix remaining relative imports <!--Separator--> Before: ```python import document.update_matching_blocks.update_matching_blocks as update_matching_blocks import document.autocomplete.autocomplete as autocomplete from helpers.observable import Observable from app.service_locator import ServiceLocator from app.color_manager import ColorManager from app.font_manager import FontManager ```
After: ```python from .update_matching_blocks import update_matching_blocks from .autocomplete import autocomplete from helpers.observable import Observable from app.service_locator import ServiceLocator from app.color_manager import ColorManager from app.font_manager import FontManager ``` </llm-patch>
The issue you're encountering is a common Python import problem. The error message "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'document.document_controller'; 'document' is not a package" indicates that Python is trying to interpret "document" as a package, but can't because you're already inside a file that is part of that package.
When a Python file imports with a syntax like `import document.document_controller`, it's looking for a package named "document" with a module inside it called "document_controller". However, when this import is being run from inside the document package itself (like your document.py file), it creates a circular reference.
The solution is to use relative imports instead of absolute imports. In Python, relative imports use dots to indicate how to navigate the package hierarchy: - `.module_name` means "look for module_name in the same directory as this file" - `..module_name` means "go up one directory level, then look for module_name"
By changing the imports to relative format, we're telling Python to look for these modules relative to the current file's location, rather than trying to start from the project root again, which avoids the circular import problem.
The fixed code should now run without the ModuleNotFoundError.

option.value:
Hello! I see you're encountering an `ImportError` in your Python script. I can certainly help you understand and fix this issue.
The error message `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` typically occurs when a Python script that is part of a package (and thus uses relative imports like `from . import ...`) is run directly. When a file is executed as the top-level script, Python doesn't know what "package" it belongs to, so the `.` (which means "the current package") in a relative import cannot be resolved.
In your case, the line `from . import document_controller` in `document.py` is causing this issue because `document.py` is being run directly.
**How to fix it:**
Assuming `document_controller.py` is a file located in the same directory as `document.py`, you can change the relative import to a direct import. This will allow Python to find and load `document_controller` when `document.py` is executed as the main script.
You would change this line: ```python from . import document_controller ``` to this: ```python import document_controller ```
This modification tells Python to look for a module named `document_controller` in the standard import paths, which includes the directory of the currently running script.
Here's how your `document.py` file might look with the fix. I've created a small example structure, placing the corrected import around line 26 as indicated in your traceback:
<llm-snippet-file>document.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python # document.py
# This is a placeholder for any code you might have # at the beginning of your document.py file. # ... (imagine this fills up to line 24) # ... # ...
# Line 26 (approximately, as per your traceback) # Original problematic line in your file: # from . import document_controller # # This was causing the error: # ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package
# The fix below assumes that 'document_controller.py' # is in the same directory as 'document.py'. # We change the relative import to a direct import: import document_controller
# Example function to demonstrate that the import now works # and how you might use the 'document_controller' module. # For this example to run, 'document_controller.py' would need to exist # and define a function like 'controller_action()'. # # For example, document_controller.py could contain: # def controller_action(): # print("Action from document_controller executed!") # def use_the_controller(): print("Now trying to use the imported document_controller.") if hasattr(document_controller, 'controller_action'): document_controller.controller_action() else: print("Module 'document_controller' imported, but 'controller_action' function not found.") print("Finished using the controller.")
if __name__ == "__main__": # This block runs if document.py is executed directly print("Starting execution of document.py...") use_the_controller() print("Execution of document.py finished.")
```
**Important Considerations:**
1. **`document_controller.py` Location:** This fix assumes that `document_controller.py` is in the same directory as `document.py`. If it's located elsewhere (e.g., in a subdirectory or a different path entirely), you'll need to adjust the import statement or your Python path accordingly. 2. **Running as a Package Module:** If `document.py` is actually intended to be part of a larger package and *not* run directly, the original relative import (`from . import document_controller`) would be correct *when `document.py` is imported as a module from within that package*. In such a scenario, the issue would be how you're running the script (e.g., you might need to run it using `python -m your_package.document`). However, since the request is to fix the code to resolve the current runtime error when run directly, the change to a direct import is the appropriate solution.
I hope this helps you resolve the import error! Let me know if you have any more questions.

self.secondary_click_controller = Gtk.GestureClick() self.secondary_click_controller.set_button(3) self.secondary_click_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.TARGET) self.secondary_click_controller.connect('pressed', self.on_secondary_buttonpress) self.view.source_view.add_controller(self.secondary_click_controller)

key_controller = Gtk.EventControllerKey() key_controller.connect('key-pressed', self.on_keypress) key_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.CAPTURE) self.document.view.source_view.add_controller(key_controller)
def on_primary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: if controller.get_current_event_state() & modifiers == Gdk.ModifierType.CONTROL_MASK: GLib.idle_add(ServiceLocator.get_workspace().actions.forward_sync)
def on_secondary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: ServiceLocator.get_workspace().context_menu.popup_at_cursor(x, y) controller.reset()
def on_keypress(self, controller, keyval, keycode, state): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()

if (state & modifiers, keyval) == (Gdk.ModifierType.SHIFT_MASK, Gdk.keyval_from_name('ISO_Left_Tab')): self.document.select_previous_placeholder() if self.document.dot_selected(): return True
return False
def on_scroll(self, controller, dx, dy): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()

if self.document.get_deleted_on_disk(): self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save = True self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(True) DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_deleted_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}) elif self.document.get_changed_on_disk(): self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = True DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_changed_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}, self.changed_on_disk_cb)

On Fedora, you can install these dependencies using the `dnf` package manager. You'll need the Python 3 bindings for GObject and the development files for GTK4.
```bash #!/bin/bash
# Update package list (optional, but good practice) sudo dnf check-update
# Install Python 3 GObject introspection bindings and GTK4 development files sudo dnf install python3-gobject gtk4-devel

Hello! I can certainly help you understand and fix this `ModuleNotFoundError`.
Let's break down the problem based on your console output:
**Understanding the Error**
The error message `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'workspace.workspace_presenter'; 'workspace' is not a package` tells us a few key things:
1. Your script, located at `/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/setzer/workspace/workspace.py`, is trying to execute the line: `import workspace.workspace_presenter as workspace_presenter` 2. When Python sees `import workspace.workspace_presenter`, it first looks for a module or package named `workspace`. 3. In this case, Python finds your file `workspace.py` and considers *it* to be the `workspace` module. 4. Then, Python tries to find `workspace_presenter` *inside* this `workspace` module (your `workspace.py` file). 5. However, a single Python file (a module) cannot also act as a package (a collection of modules, often represented by a directory with an `__init__.py` file). This is why you get the specific error: `'workspace' is not a package`. Your `workspace.py` file is a module, not a package that can contain `workspace_presenter`.
This is a common issue when a script's name (`workspace.py`) conflicts with the name of a package it's trying to import from, or when the import statement doesn't correctly reflect the project structure.
**Solution**

You're right to point out the structure of the `main.py` file. While there isn't a function explicitly defined as `def main():`, the script uses a standard Python construct to define its entry point.
In Python, the block of code under `if __name__ == "__main__":` is executed when the script is run directly. In your `main.py` file, this section is:
<llm-snippet-file>main.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python if __name__ == "__main__": app = SetzerApplication() exit_status = app.run(sys.argv) sys.exit(exit_status) ```
This is the main execution flow of your application: 1. An instance of `SetzerApplication` is created. 2. The `app.run(sys.argv)` method is called, which starts the GTK application loop. 3. The script exits with the status returned by the application.
The actual setup and activation of the application's components, like initializing services and creating the main window, happen within the `SetzerApplication` class, particularly in its `do_activate` method:
<llm-snippet-file>main.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python class SetzerApplication(Gtk.Application): """Main application class for Setzer"""
def __init__(self): super().__init__(application_id="org.setzer.app", flags=Gio.ApplicationFlags.FLAGS_NONE)
def do_activate(self): # Initialize application services if hasattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services') and callable(getattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services')): ServiceLocator.init_services() else: # It's good practice to log or warn that a potentially important step is skipped. print("Warning: ServiceLocator.init_services() method not found or not callable. " "Application services may not be fully initialized.", file=sys.stderr) # Depending on the criticality, you might want to raise an error or exit. # For now, we'll let it proceed, assuming get_main_window might still work # or that init_services was for non-critical components.
# Create the main window main_window = ServiceLocator.get_main_window() # This call might fail if init_services was critical and not called self.add_window(main_window) main_window.present()
# Initialize workspace workspace = Workspace() self.controller = WorkspaceController(workspace) ```
So, while there isn't a separate function named `main`, the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block serves as the primary entry point, and the `SetzerApplication.do_activate` method handles the application's initialization logic. This is a perfectly valid and common way to structure Python applications.
If you were expecting a `def main():` function, this is a stylistic choice some developers make to encapsulate the main script logic, but it's not a requirement for a Python script to run.

It's common for a GUI application to show no window and no errors if the main window is created but its content isn't properly initialized or displayed.
Looking at your `main.py` and the provided `MainWindow` class from `workspace_viewgtk.py`, a likely cause is that the `create_widgets()` method of your `MainWindow` is not being called.
Here's the relevant part of `SetzerApplication.do_activate` in `main.py`: <llm-snippet-file>main.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python def do_activate(self): # Initialize application services if hasattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services') and callable(getattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services')): ServiceLocator.init_services() else: # ... (warning print)
# Create the main window main_window = ServiceLocator.get_main_window() # This call might fail if init_services was critical and not called self.add_window(main_window) main_window.present()
# Initialize workspace workspace = Workspace() self.controller = WorkspaceController(workspace) ```
And here's the structure of your `MainWindow` from `workspace_viewgtk.py`: ```python class MainWindow(Adw.ApplicationWindow): def __init__(self, app): Adw.ApplicationWindow.__init__(self, application=app) # ... self.popoverlay = Gtk.Overlay() self.set_content(self.popoverlay) # Window content is an empty overlay initially # ... NO CALL to self.create_widgets() here
def create_widgets(self): # ... self.main_box = Gtk.Box.new(Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL, 0) # ... (main_box gets populated) ... self.popoverlay.set_child(self.main_box) # popoverlay gets its actual content here # ... ```
The `MainWindow.__init__` method sets an empty `Gtk.Overlay` as the window's content. The `create_widgets()` method is responsible for creating the actual UI elements (like `main_box`) and adding them to this overlay. If `create_widgets()` is never called on the `main_window` instance, the window will remain effectively empty, which can lead to it not being displayed or appearing as a blank, unusable window.
The `ServiceLocator.get_main_window()` call retrieves the main window instance. It's crucial that `create_widgets()` is called on this instance. This could either happen within `ServiceLocator.init_services()` or `ServiceLocator.get_main_window()`, or it needs to be done explicitly in `do_activate`.
Assuming `ServiceLocator` doesn't call `create_widgets()` internally, you should call it in `do_activate` after retrieving the window. It's also good practice to check if `main_window` was successfully retrieved.
Here's a suggested modification to your `SetzerApplication.do_activate` method in `main.py`:
<llm-snippet-file>main.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python def do_activate(self): # Initialize application services if hasattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services') and callable(getattr(ServiceLocator, 'init_services')): ServiceLocator.init_services() else: # It's good practice to log or warn that a potentially important step is skipped. print("Warning: ServiceLocator.init_services() method not found or not callable. " "Application services may not be fully initialized.", file=sys.stderr) # Depending on the criticality, you might want to raise an error or exit. # For now, we'll let it proceed, assuming get_main_window might still work # or that init_services was for non-critical components.
# Get the main window main_window = ServiceLocator.get_main_window()
if not main_window: print("Critical Error: ServiceLocator.get_main_window() returned None. UI cannot be initialized.", file=sys.stderr) # Consider a clean exit if the application cannot proceed without a main window if hasattr(self, 'quit'): self.quit() sys.exit(1) # Exit if no main window
# Ensure widgets are created for the main window if hasattr(main_window, 'create_widgets') and callable(getattr(main_window, 'create_widgets')): main_window.create_widgets() else: print("Warning: main_window does not have a callable create_widgets method. UI might be incomplete.", file=sys.stderr)
self.add_window(main_window) main_window.present()
# Initialize workspace workspace = Workspace() self.controller = WorkspaceController(workspace) ```
**Key changes and why:** 1. **Check `main_window`**: Added a check to ensure `ServiceLocator.get_main_window()` actually returns a window object. If it's `None`, the application can't proceed, and it prints an error and exits. 2. **Call `main_window.create_widgets()`**: This is the crucial part. If `main_window` is valid and has a `create_widgets` method (which it should, if it's an instance of your `MainWindow` class), this line calls it. This will populate the window with its UI elements.
Try applying this change. If the window still doesn't appear, or if you see new errors or warnings (e.g., "main_window does not have a callable create_widgets method"), it will provide more clues about where the issue might be (e.g., `ServiceLocator.get_main_window()` might be returning something unexpected, or an error occurs within `create_widgets` itself).

```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # coding: utf-8

import os.path
import gi gi.require_version('Gtk', '4.0') from gi.repository import Gdk, GLib, Gtk, GObject, Pango
from setzer.dialogs.dialog_locator import DialogLocator from setzer.app.service_locator import ServiceLocator from setzer.app.font_manager import FontManager
class DocumentController(object):
def __init__(self, document, document_view):
self.document = document self.view = document_view
self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save = False self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = False self.continue_save_date_loop = True self.zoom_threshold = 0 GObject.timeout_add(500, self.save_date_loop)
self.primary_click_controller = Gtk.GestureClick() self.primary_click_controller.set_button(1) self.primary_click_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.TARGET) self.primary_click_controller.connect('pressed', self.on_primary_buttonpress) self.view.source_view.add_controller(self.primary_click_controller)
self.secondary_click_controller = Gtk.GestureClick() self.secondary_click_controller.set_button(3) self.secondary_click_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.TARGET) self.secondary_click_controller.connect('pressed', self.on_secondary_buttonpress) self.view.source_view.add_controller(self.secondary_click_controller)
self.scrolling_controller = Gtk.EventControllerScroll() self.scrolling_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.CAPTURE) self.scrolling_controller.set_flags(Gtk.EventControllerScrollFlags.BOTH_AXES | Gtk.EventControllerScrollFlags.KINETIC) self.scrolling_controller.connect('scroll', self.on_scroll) self.scrolling_controller.connect('decelerate', self.on_decelerate) self.view.scrolled_window.add_controller(self.scrolling_controller)
key_controller = Gtk.EventControllerKey() key_controller.connect('key-pressed', self.on_keypress) key_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.CAPTURE) self.document.view.source_view.add_controller(key_controller)
def on_primary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: if controller.get_current_event_state() & modifiers == Gdk.ModifierType.CONTROL_MASK: GLib.idle_add(ServiceLocator.get_workspace().actions.forward_sync)
def on_secondary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: ServiceLocator.get_workspace().context_menu.popup_at_cursor(x, y) controller.reset()
def on_keypress(self, controller, keyval, keycode, state): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if keyval in [Gdk.keyval_from_name('Tab'), Gdk.keyval_from_name('ISO_Left_Tab')]: if state & modifiers == 0: self.document.select_next_placeholder() if self.document.dot_selected(): return True
if not self.document.settings.get_value('preferences', 'tab_jump_brackets'): return False chars_at_cursor = self.document.get_chars_at_cursor(2) if chars_at_cursor in ['\\}', '\\)', '\\]']: forward_chars = 2 elif chars_at_cursor[0] in ['}', ')', ']']: forward_chars = 1 else: return False
insert_iter = self.document.source_buffer.get_iter_at_mark(self.document.source_buffer.get_insert()) insert_iter.forward_chars(forward_chars) self.document.source_buffer.place_cursor(insert_iter) return True
if (state & modifiers, keyval) == (Gdk.ModifierType.SHIFT_MASK, Gdk.keyval_from_name('ISO_Left_Tab')): self.document.select_previous_placeholder() if self.document.dot_selected(): return True
return False
def on_scroll(self, controller, dx, dy): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if controller.get_current_event_state() & modifiers == Gdk.ModifierType.CONTROL_MASK: if controller.get_unit() == Gdk.ScrollUnit.WHEEL: self.zoom_threshold += dy else: self.zoom_threshold += dy * 0.05
if self.zoom_threshold <= -1: font_desc = Pango.FontDescription.from_string(FontManager.font_string) font_desc.set_size(min(font_desc.get_size() * 1.1, 24 * Pango.SCALE)) FontManager.font_string = font_desc.to_string() FontManager.propagate_font_setting() self.zoom_threshold = 0 elif self.zoom_threshold >= 1: font_desc = Pango.FontDescription.from_string(FontManager.font_string) font_desc.set_size(max(font_desc.get_size() / 1.1, 6 * Pango.SCALE)) FontManager.font_string = font_desc.to_string() FontManager.propagate_font_setting() self.zoom_threshold = 0 return True return False
def on_decelerate(self, controller, vel_x, vel_y): self.zoom_threshold = 0
def save_date_loop(self): if self.document.filename == None: return True if self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save: return True if self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change: return True
if self.document.get_deleted_on_disk(): self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save = True self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(True) DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_deleted_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}) elif self.document.get_changed_on_disk(): self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = True DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_changed_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}, self.changed_on_disk_cb)
return self.continue_save_date_loop
def changed_on_disk_cb(self, do_reload): if do_reload: self.document.populate_from_filename() self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(False) else: self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(True) self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = False self.document.update_save_date()

# Set up a timeout to keep the application running def keep_app_alive(): # Keep the application running return True # Return True to keep the timeout active

import gi gi.require_version('GtkSource', '5') from gi.repository import GtkSource from gi.repository import GLib
import re import os, os.path import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import setzer.settings.settings as settingscontroller
class ServiceLocator():
main_window = None workspace = None settings = None setzer_version = None resources_path = None app_icons_path = None increments = dict() regexes = dict() source_language_manager = None source_style_scheme_manager = None
def set_main_window(main_window): ServiceLocator.main_window = main_window
def get_main_window(): return ServiceLocator.main_window
def set_workspace(workspace): ServiceLocator.workspace = workspace
def get_workspace(): return ServiceLocator.workspace
def get_increment(key): if key not in ServiceLocator.increments: ServiceLocator.increments[key] = 0 ServiceLocator.increments[key] += 1 return ServiceLocator.increments[key]
def get_regex_object(pattern): if pattern in ServiceLocator.regexes: return ServiceLocator.regexes[pattern] else: regex = re.compile(pattern) ServiceLocator.regexes[pattern] = regex return regex
def get_settings(): if ServiceLocator.settings == None: ServiceLocator.settings = settingscontroller.Settings(ServiceLocator.get_config_folder()) return ServiceLocator.settings
def get_config_folder(): return os.path.join(GLib.get_user_config_dir(), 'setzer')
def set_setzer_version(setzer_version): ServiceLocator.setzer_version = setzer_version
def get_setzer_version(): return ServiceLocator.setzer_version
def set_resources_path(resources_path): ServiceLocator.resources_path = resources_path
def get_resources_path(): return ServiceLocator.resources_path
def set_app_icons_path(app_icons_path): ServiceLocator.app_icons_path = app_icons_path
def get_app_icons_path(): return ServiceLocator.app_icons_path
def get_source_language_manager(): if ServiceLocator.source_language_manager == None: ServiceLocator.source_language_manager = GtkSource.LanguageManager() path = os.path.join(ServiceLocator.get_resources_path(), 'language-specs') ServiceLocator.source_language_manager.set_search_path((path,)) return ServiceLocator.source_language_manager
def get_source_style_scheme_manager(): if ServiceLocator.source_style_scheme_manager == None: ServiceLocator.source_style_scheme_manager = GtkSource.StyleSchemeManager() path1 = os.path.join(ServiceLocator.get_resources_path(), 'themes') if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(ServiceLocator.get_config_folder(), 'themes')): os.mkdir(os.path.join(ServiceLocator.get_config_folder(), 'themes')) path2 = os.path.join(ServiceLocator.get_config_folder(), 'themes') ServiceLocator.source_style_scheme_manager.set_search_path((path1, path2)) return ServiceLocator.source_style_scheme_manager
def get_source_language(language): source_language_manager = ServiceLocator.get_source_language_manager() if language == 'bibtex': return source_language_manager.get_language('bibtex') else: return source_language_manager.get_language('latex')

# Create main window app = Gtk.Application.get_default() main_window = MainWindow(app) ServiceLocator.set_main_window(main_window)

app_icons_path = os.path.join(resources_path, 'icons') ServiceLocator.set_app_icons_path(app_icons_path)
return True

from setzer.dialogs.dialog_locator import DialogLocator from setzer.app.service_locator import ServiceLocator from setzer.app.font_manager import FontManager
class DocumentController(object):
def __init__(self, document, document_view):
self.document = document self.view = document_view
self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save = False self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = False self.continue_save_date_loop = True self.zoom_threshold = 0 GObject.timeout_add(500, self.save_date_loop)
self.primary_click_controller = Gtk.GestureClick() self.primary_click_controller.set_button(1) self.primary_click_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.TARGET) self.primary_click_controller.connect('pressed', self.on_primary_buttonpress) self.view.source_view.add_controller(self.primary_click_controller)
self.secondary_click_controller = Gtk.GestureClick() self.secondary_click_controller.set_button(3) self.secondary_click_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.TARGET) self.secondary_click_controller.connect('pressed', self.on_secondary_buttonpress) self.view.source_view.add_controller(self.secondary_click_controller)
self.scrolling_controller = Gtk.EventControllerScroll() self.scrolling_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.CAPTURE) self.scrolling_controller.set_flags(Gtk.EventControllerScrollFlags.BOTH_AXES | Gtk.EventControllerScrollFlags.KINETIC) self.scrolling_controller.connect('scroll', self.on_scroll) self.scrolling_controller.connect('decelerate', self.on_decelerate) self.view.scrolled_window.add_controller(self.scrolling_controller)
key_controller = Gtk.EventControllerKey() key_controller.connect('key-pressed', self.on_keypress) key_controller.set_propagation_phase(Gtk.PropagationPhase.CAPTURE) self.document.view.source_view.add_controller(key_controller)
def on_primary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: if controller.get_current_event_state() & modifiers == Gdk.ModifierType.CONTROL_MASK: GLib.idle_add(ServiceLocator.get_workspace().actions.forward_sync)
def on_secondary_buttonpress(self, controller, n_press, x, y): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if n_press == 1: ServiceLocator.get_workspace().context_menu.popup_at_cursor(x, y) controller.reset()
def on_keypress(self, controller, keyval, keycode, state): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if keyval in [Gdk.keyval_from_name('Tab'), Gdk.keyval_from_name('ISO_Left_Tab')]: if state & modifiers == 0: self.document.select_next_placeholder() if self.document.dot_selected(): return True
if not self.document.settings.get_value('preferences', 'tab_jump_brackets'): return False chars_at_cursor = self.document.get_chars_at_cursor(2) if chars_at_cursor in ['\\}', '\\)', '\\]']: forward_chars = 2 elif chars_at_cursor[0] in ['}', ')', ']']: forward_chars = 1 else: return False
insert_iter = self.document.source_buffer.get_iter_at_mark(self.document.source_buffer.get_insert()) insert_iter.forward_chars(forward_chars) self.document.source_buffer.place_cursor(insert_iter) return True
if (state & modifiers, keyval) == (Gdk.ModifierType.SHIFT_MASK, Gdk.keyval_from_name('ISO_Left_Tab')): self.document.select_previous_placeholder() if self.document.dot_selected(): return True
return False
def on_scroll(self, controller, dx, dy): modifiers = Gtk.accelerator_get_default_mod_mask()
if controller.get_current_event_state() & modifiers == Gdk.ModifierType.CONTROL_MASK: if controller.get_unit() == Gdk.ScrollUnit.WHEEL: self.zoom_threshold += dy else: self.zoom_threshold += dy * 0.05
if self.zoom_threshold <= -1: font_desc = Pango.FontDescription.from_string(FontManager.font_string) font_desc.set_size(min(font_desc.get_size() * 1.1, 24 * Pango.SCALE)) FontManager.font_string = font_desc.to_string() FontManager.propagate_font_setting() self.zoom_threshold = 0 elif self.zoom_threshold >= 1: font_desc = Pango.FontDescription.from_string(FontManager.font_string) font_desc.set_size(max(font_desc.get_size() / 1.1, 6 * Pango.SCALE)) FontManager.font_string = font_desc.to_string() FontManager.propagate_font_setting() self.zoom_threshold = 0 return True return False
def on_decelerate(self, controller, vel_x, vel_y): self.zoom_threshold = 0
def save_date_loop(self): if self.document.filename == None: return True if self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save: return True if self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change: return True
if self.document.get_deleted_on_disk(): self.deleted_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_save = True self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(True) DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_deleted_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}) elif self.document.get_changed_on_disk(): self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = True DialogLocator.get_dialog('document_changed_on_disk').run({'document': self.document}, self.changed_on_disk_cb)
return self.continue_save_date_loop
def changed_on_disk_cb(self, do_reload): if do_reload: self.document.populate_from_filename() self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(False) else: self.document.source_buffer.set_modified(True) self.changed_on_disk_dialog_shown_after_last_change = False self.document.update_save_date()
```

Hello! I've analyzed the console output you provided. It seems like the program is crashing because of a `NameError`. Specifically, the name `_` is not defined in the file `/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/setzer/popovers/shortcutsbar/quotes_menu.py`.
This `_` is conventionally used as an alias for the `gettext` function, which is used for internationalization and localization (translating text in applications).
The error occurs on line 41 of `quotes_menu.py`: ```python self.add_before_after_item('main', _('Primary Quotes') + ' (`` ... \'\')', ['``', '\'\'']) ``` Here, `_('Primary Quotes')` is an attempt to call the translation function, but it hasn't been defined or imported in this file.
To fix this, we need to import the `gettext` module and assign its `gettext` function to `_` at the beginning of the `quotes_menu.py` file.
Here's the suggested modification: <llm-snippet-file>/home/xxx/IdeaProjects/silly/setzer/popovers/shortcutsbar/quotes_menu.py</llm-snippet-file> ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # coding: utf-8

import gi gi.require_version('Gtk', '4.0') from gi.repository import Gtk from gi.repository import GLib
import gettext _ = gettext.gettext
from setzer.popovers.helpers.popover_menu_builder import MenuBuilder from setzer.popovers.helpers.popover import Popover
class QuotesMenu(object):
def __init__(self, popover_manager): self.view = QuotesMenuView(popover_manager)
class QuotesMenuView(Popover):
def __init__(self, popover_manager): Popover.__init__(self, popover_manager) self.get_style_context().add_class('menu-own-quotes-symbolic')
self.set_width(288)
self.add_before_after_item('main', _('Primary Quotes') + ' (`` ... \'\')', ['``', '\'\'']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('Secondary Quotes') + ' (` ... \')', ['`', '\'']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('German Quotes') + ' (\\glqq ... \\grqq{})', ['\\glqq ', '\\grqq{}']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('German Single Quotes') + ' (\\glq ... \\grq{})', ['\\glq ', '\\grq{}']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('French Quotes') + ' (\\flqq ... \\frqq{})', ['\\flqq ', '\\frqq{}']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('French Single Quotes') + ' (\\flq ... \\frq{})', ['\\flq ', '\\frq{}']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('German Alt Quotes') + ' (\\frqq ... \\flqq{})', ['\\frqq ', '\\flqq{}']) self.add_before_after_item('main', _('German Alt Single Quotes') + ' (\\frq ... \\frq{})', ['\\frq ', '\\flq{}'])
``` By adding these two lines: ```python import gettext _ = gettext.gettext ``` the `_` function will be properly defined, and the `NameError` should be resolved. This is a long-term solution as it correctly sets up the translation mechanism expected by the code.

It's a GTK-based Python application that was originally designed to be built and run using the Meson build system. You want to run it directly as a Python application, and I can help you with the common steps to achieve that.
Running a Python application directly when it's designed for a build system like Meson involves a few key considerations:
1. **Resource Management**: Meson typically handles packaging and locating resource files (like CSS stylesheets, icons, etc.). When running directly, the application needs to be able to find these files. Your `workspace_viewgtk.py` specifically tries to load `style_gtk.css` using `ServiceLocator.get_resources_path()`. The fallback logic in your `main.py` for setting this path needs to correctly point to where your resources are located in your source tree. 2. **Python Module Resolution**: Python needs to be able to find your project's modules (e.g., the `setzer` package). Running your main script from the project's root directory usually handles this. 3. **Internationalization (i18n)**: The `_()` function is used for translating strings. If `gettext` is not properly initialized in each file that uses `_()`, you'll get `NameError` exceptions. We fixed one instance of this in `quotes_menu.py` previously. 4. **Dependencies**: Ensure all necessary Python libraries and GTK bindings (`Gtk 4.0`, `Adw 1`) are installed and accessible in your Python environment.
Based on the provided code and typical Python project structures for applications like Setzer, here's how we can address these points to get your application running:
**1. Adjust Resource Path Loading in `main.py`**
The current fallback logic in your `main.py` for determining `resources_path` is likely incorrect if `main.py` is in the root directory of your project. It calculates the path as `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'resources')`, which would look for a `resources` directory *outside* your project folder.

try: self.main_window.headerbar.preview_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_preview_toggle_toggled) self.main_window.headerbar.help_toggle.connect('toggled', self.on_help_toggle_toggled)

if show_help: self.main_window.headerbar.preview_toggle.set_active(False)

Adjust if necessary. resources_path = os.path.join(project_root_dir, 'data') if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(resources_path, 'style_gtk.css')): # Fallback for another common structure like 'PROJECT_ROOT/resources/style_gtk.css' resources_path_alt = os.path.join(project_root_dir, 'resources') if os.path.exists(os.path.join(resources_path_alt, 'style_gtk.css')): resources_path = resources_path_alt else: print(f"Warning: Could not find 'style_gtk.css' in '{resources_path}' or '{resources_path_alt}'. UI might be incomplete.", file=sys.stderr)
print("Adding window to application", file=sys.stderr) self.add_window(main_window) self._windows.append(main_window) # Prevent garbage collection
print("Setting window properties", file=sys.stderr) main_window.set_default_size(1200, 800) main_window.set_title("Setzer LaTeX Editor")
print("Presenting window", file=sys.stderr) main_window.present()

class PopoverManager():
popovers = dict() popover_buttons = dict() current_popover_name = None main_window = None workspace = None popoverlay = None inbetween = Gtk.DrawingArea()
connected_functions = dict() # observers' functions to be called when change codes are emitted
def init(main_window, workspace): PopoverManager.main_window = main_window PopoverManager.workspace = workspace PopoverManager.popoverlay = main_window.popoverlay PopoverManager.popoverlay.add_overlay(PopoverManager.inbetween)
controller_click = Gtk.GestureClick() controller_click.connect('pressed', PopoverManager.on_click_inbetween) controller_click.set_button(1) PopoverManager.inbetween.add_controller(controller_click)
PopoverManager.inbetween.set_can_target(False)
def create_popover(name): popover = None if name == 'new_document': popover = NewDocument(PopoverManager) if name == 'open_document': popover = DocumentChooser(PopoverManager, PopoverManager.workspace) if name == 'document_switcher': popover = DocumentSwitcher(PopoverManager, PopoverManager.workspace) if name == 'hamburger_menu': popover = HamburgerMenu(PopoverManager, PopoverManager.workspace) if name == 'beamer_menu': popover = BeamerMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'bibliography_menu': popover = BibliographyMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'document_menu': popover = DocumentMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'math_menu': popover = MathMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'object_menu': popover = ObjectMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'quotes_menu': popover = QuotesMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'text_menu': popover = TextMenu(PopoverManager) if name == 'preview_zoom_level': popover = PreviewZoomLevel(PopoverManager, PopoverManager.workspace) if name == 'context_menu': popover = ContextMenu(PopoverManager, PopoverManager.workspace)
PopoverManager.popovers[name] = popover return popover
def create_popover_button(name): popover_button = PopoverButton(name, PopoverManager) PopoverManager.popover_buttons[name] = popover_button return popover_button
def popup_at_button(name): if PopoverManager.current_popover_name == name: return if PopoverManager.current_popover_name != None: PopoverManager.popdown()
button = PopoverManager.popover_buttons[name] allocation = button.compute_bounds(PopoverManager.main_window).out_bounds
x = allocation.origin.x + allocation.size.width / 2 y = allocation.origin.y + allocation.size.height
popover = PopoverManager.popovers[name] window_width = PopoverManager.main_window.get_width() arrow_width = 10 arrow_border_width = 36 if x - popover.view.width / 2 < 0: popover.view.set_margin_start(0) popover.view.arrow.set_margin_start(x - arrow_width / 2) popover.view.arrow_border.set_margin_start(x - arrow_border_width / 2) elif x - popover.view.width / 2 > window_width - popover.view.width: popover.view.set_margin_start(window_width - popover.view.width) popover.view.arrow.set_margin_start(x - window_width + popover.view.width - arrow_width / 2) popover.view.arrow_border.set_margin_start(x - window_width + popover.view.width - arrow_border_width / 2) else: popover.view.set_margin_start(x - popover.view.width / 2) popover.view.arrow.set_margin_start(popover.view.width / 2 - arrow_width / 2) popover.view.arrow_border.set_margin_start(popover.view.width / 2 - arrow_border_width / 2) popover.view.set_margin_top(max(0, y))
PopoverManager.current_popover_name = name PopoverManager.popoverlay.add_overlay(popover.view) PopoverManager.inbetween.set_can_target(True)
popover.view.grab_focus() button.set_active(True)
PopoverManager.add_change_code('popup', name)
def popdown(): if PopoverManager.current_popover_name == None: return
name = PopoverManager.current_popover_name popover = PopoverManager.popovers[name]
PopoverManager.popoverlay.remove_overlay(popover.view) PopoverManager.current_popover_name = None PopoverManager.inbetween.set_can_target(False)
popover.view.show_page(None, 'main', Gtk.StackTransitionType.NONE) if name in PopoverManager.popover_buttons: PopoverManager.popover_buttons[name].set_active(False)
document = PopoverManager.workspace.get_active_document() if document != None: document.source_view.grab_focus()
PopoverManager.add_change_code('popdown', name)
def on_click_inbetween(controller, n_press, x, y): PopoverManager.popdown()
def add_change_code(change_code, parameter=None): if change_code in PopoverManager.connected_functions: for callback in PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code]: if parameter != None: callback(parameter) else: callback()
def connect(change_code, callback): if change_code in PopoverManager.connected_functions: PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code].add(callback) else: PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code] = {callback}
def disconnect(change_code, callback): if change_code in PopoverManager.connected_functions: PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code].discard(callback) if len(PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code]) == 0: del(PopoverManager.connected_functions[change_code])
